claim: Neurofibromatosis type 1 (NF1) is characterized by nerve tumors called neurofibromas, in which Schwann cells (SCs) show deregulated RAS signaling.
source: Neurofibromatosis type 1 (NF1) is characterized by nerve tumors called neurofibromas, in which Schwann cells (SCs) show deregulated RAS signaling.
evidence: This is a well-established characteristic of NF1 based on scientific consensus and prior research.

claim: NF1 is implicated in regulation of cAMP.
source: NF1 is also implicated in regulation of cAMP.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about NF1.

claim: P2ry14 was identified in human neurofibromas.
source: We identified the G-protein-coupled receptor (GPCR) P2ry14 in human neurofibromas, neurofibroma-derived SC precursors (SCPs), mature SCs, and mouse SCPs.
evidence: The manuscript presents experimental data showing P2ry14 expression in human neurofibromas through multiple methods including microarray, Western blot, and immunohistochemistry.

claim: P2ry14 was identified in neurofibroma-derived SC precursors (SCPs).
source: We identified the G-protein-coupled receptor (GPCR) P2ry14 in human neurofibromas, neurofibroma-derived SC precursors (SCPs), mature SCs, and mouse SCPs.
evidence: The manuscript presents experimental data showing P2ry14 expression in SCPs through FACS analysis and Western blot.

claim: P2ry14 was identified in mature SCs.
source: We identified the G-protein-coupled receptor (GPCR) P2ry14 in human neurofibromas, neurofibroma-derived SC precursors (SCPs), mature SCs, and mouse SCPs.
evidence: The manuscript presents experimental data showing P2ry14 expression in mature SCs through Western blot and immunostaining.

claim: P2ry14 was identified in mouse SCPs.
source: We identified the G-protein-coupled receptor (GPCR) P2ry14 in human neurofibromas, neurofibroma-derived SC precursors (SCPs), mature SCs, and mouse SCPs.
evidence: The manuscript presents experimental data showing P2ry14 expression in mouse SCPs through β-galactosidase reporter and immunostaining.

claim: Mouse Nf1-/- SCP self-renewal was reduced by genetic inhibition of P2ry14.
source: Mouse Nf1-/- SCP self-renewal was reduced by genetic or pharmacological inhibition of P2ry14.
evidence: The manuscript presents sphere formation assay data showing reduced self-renewal with shRNA targeting P2ry14.

claim: Mouse Nf1-/- SCP self-renewal was reduced by pharmacological inhibition of P2ry14.
source: Mouse Nf1-/- SCP self-renewal was reduced by genetic or pharmacological inhibition of P2ry14.
evidence: The manuscript presents sphere formation assay data showing reduced self-renewal with PPTN treatment.

claim: Genetic deletion of P2ry14 rescued low cAMP signaling in a mouse model of NF1.
source: In a mouse model of NF1, genetic deletion of P2ry14 rescued low cAMP signaling, increased mouse survival, delayed neurofibroma initiation, and improved SC Remak bundles.
evidence: The manuscript presents data showing increased p-PKA substrate phosphorylation in P2ry14-/-;Nf1fl/fl;DhhCre mice compared to Nf1fl/fl;DhhCre mice.

claim: Genetic deletion of P2ry14 increased mouse survival in a mouse model of NF1.
source: In a mouse model of NF1, genetic deletion of P2ry14 rescued low cAMP signaling, increased mouse survival, delayed neurofibroma initiation, and improved SC Remak bundles.
evidence: The manuscript presents Kaplan-Meier survival analysis showing significantly increased survival in P2ry14-/-;Nf1fl/fl;DhhCre mice.

claim: Genetic deletion of P2ry14 delayed neurofibroma initiation in a mouse model of NF1.
source: In a mouse model of NF1, genetic deletion of P2ry14 rescued low cAMP signaling, increased mouse survival, delayed neurofibroma initiation, and improved SC Remak bundles.
evidence: The manuscript presents data showing decreased neurofibroma number in P2ry14-/-;Nf1fl/fl;DhhCre mice at 4 and 7 months.

claim: Genetic deletion of P2ry14 improved SC Remak bundles in a mouse model of NF1.
source: In a mouse model of NF1, genetic deletion of P2ry14 rescued low cAMP signaling, increased mouse survival, delayed neurofibroma initiation, and improved SC Remak bundles.
evidence: The manuscript presents electron microscopy data showing improved Remak bundle morphology in P2ry14-/-;Nf1fl/fl;DhhCre mice.

claim: P2ry14 signals via Gi to increase intracellular cAMP.
source: P2ry14 signals via Gi to increase intracellular cAMP, implicating P2ry14 as a key upstream regulator of cAMP.
evidence: The manuscript presents data showing that P2ry14 inhibition or knockdown increases pPKA substrate phosphorylation, an indirect measure of cAMP levels.

claim: P2ry14 is a key upstream regulator of cAMP.
source: P2ry14 signals via Gi to increase intracellular cAMP, implicating P2ry14 as a key upstream regulator of cAMP.
evidence: This is inferred from the experimental data showing that P2ry14 inhibition affects cAMP signaling.

claim: Elevation of cAMP by blocking the degradation of cAMP diminished NF1-/- SCP self-renewal in vitro.
source: We found that elevation of cAMP by either blocking the degradation of cAMP or by using a P2ry14 inhibitor diminished NF1-/- SCP self-renewal in vitro and neurofibroma SC proliferation in in vivo.
evidence: The manuscript presents sphere formation assay data showing reduced self-renewal with rolipram treatment.

claim: Elevation of cAMP by using a P2ry14 inhibitor diminished NF1-/- SCP self-renewal in vitro.
source: We found that elevation of cAMP by either blocking the degradation of cAMP or by using a P2ry14 inhibitor diminished NF1-/- SCP self-renewal in vitro and neurofibroma SC proliferation in in vivo.
evidence: The manuscript presents sphere formation assay data showing reduced self-renewal with PPTN treatment.

claim: Elevation of cAMP by blocking the degradation of cAMP diminished neurofibroma SC proliferation in vivo.
source: We found that elevation of cAMP by either blocking the degradation of cAMP or by using a P2ry14 inhibitor diminished NF1-/- SCP self-renewal in vitro and neurofibroma SC proliferation in in vivo.
evidence: The manuscript presents Ki67 staining data showing reduced proliferation in neurofibromas after rolipram treatment.

claim: Elevation of cAMP by using a P2ry14 inhibitor diminished neurofibroma SC proliferation in vivo.
source: We found that elevation of cAMP by either blocking the degradation of cAMP or by using a P2ry14 inhibitor diminished NF1-/- SCP self-renewal in vitro and neurofibroma SC proliferation in in vivo.
evidence: The manuscript presents Ki67 staining data showing reduced proliferation in neurofibromas after PPTN treatment.

claim: P2ry14 is a critical regulator of SCP self-renewal.
source: These studies identify P2ry14 as a critical regulator of SCP self-renewal, SC proliferation, and neurofibroma initiation.
evidence: This conclusion is based on the experimental data showing effects of P2ry14 inhibition on SCP sphere formation.

claim: P2ry14 is a critical regulator of SC proliferation.
source: These studies identify P2ry14 as a critical regulator of SCP self-renewal, SC proliferation, and neurofibroma initiation.
evidence: This conclusion is based on the experimental data showing effects of P2ry14 deletion on Ki67+ cells in neurofibromas.

claim: P2ry14 is a critical regulator of neurofibroma initiation.
source: These studies identify P2ry14 as a critical regulator of SCP self-renewal, SC proliferation, and neurofibroma initiation.
evidence: This conclusion is based on the experimental data showing reduced tumor number in P2ry14 knockout mice.

claim: NF1 affects up to 1:2000 individuals worldwide.
source: Neurofibromatosis type 1 (NF1) is an autosomal dominant disease that affects up to 1:2000 individuals worldwide (Kallionpää et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Kallionpää et al., 2018.

claim: There is no cure for NF1.
source: To date, there is no cure for NF1, which is characterized by multiple, variable, clinical manifestations (Friedman, 1998; Tabata et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Friedman, 1998 and Tabata et al., 2020.

claim: At least half of the children with NF1 develop plexiform neurofibromas (PNs).
source: At least half of the children with NF1 develop plexiform neurofibromas (PNs), which are tumors within peripheral nerves.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about NF1.

claim: PN may be present at birth.
source: PN may be present at birth and show most rapid growth during the first decade of a child's life (Nguyen et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Nguyen et al., 2012.

claim: PN show most rapid growth during the first decade of a child's life.
source: PN may be present at birth and show most rapid growth during the first decade of a child's life (Nguyen et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Nguyen et al., 2012.

claim: PNs have the potential to transform into lethal malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumors (MPNST).
source: PNs can occur in any cranial or peripheral nerve and have the potential to transform into lethal malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumors (MPNST) (Prudner et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Prudner et al., 2020.

claim: Schwann cells (SCs) are the only cell type in neurofibromas that shows bi-allelic loss-of-function mutations in the NF1 tumor suppressor gene.
source: Peripheral nerve glial cells, Schwann cells (SCs), are the only cell type in neurofibromas that shows bi-allelic loss-of-function mutations in the NF1 tumor suppressor gene (Serra et al., 1997; Serra et al., 2001).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Serra et al., 1997 and Serra et al., 2001.

claim: Neurofibroma SCs show aberrant properties ex vivo.
source: Neurofibroma SCs also show aberrant properties ex vivo, consistent with it being the primary pathogenic cell type in neurofibromas (Sheela et al., 1990; Kim et al., 1995).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Sheela et al., 1990 and Kim et al., 1995.

claim: Neural crest cells develop into SC precursors (SCPs) between embryonic day 11 (E11) and E13 in mice.
source: In mice, neural crest cells develop into SC precursors (SCPs) between embryonic day 11 (E11) and E13 (Jessen and Mirsky, 2019).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Jessen and Mirsky, 2019.

claim: SCPs or related boundary cap cells can serve as cells-of-origin for neurofibromas.
source: SCPs or related boundary cap cells can serve as cells-of-origin for neurofibromas, as loss of Nf1 in these cells causes PN formation (Zhu et al., 2002; Wu et al., 2008; Chen et al., 2014; Chen et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Zhu et al., 2002; Wu et al., 2008; Chen et al., 2014; Chen et al., 2019.

claim: Loss of Nf1 in SCPs or related boundary cap cells causes PN formation.
source: SCPs or related boundary cap cells can serve as cells-of-origin for neurofibromas, as loss of Nf1 in these cells causes PN formation (Zhu et al., 2002; Wu et al., 2008; Chen et al., 2014; Chen et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Zhu et al., 2002; Wu et al., 2008; Chen et al., 2014; Chen et al., 2019.

claim: Embryonic SCPs retain multi-lineage differentiation potential and self-renewal capabilities for several passages in vitro.
source: In vitro, embryonic SCPs retain multi-lineage differentiation potential and self-renewal capabilities for several passages, indicating that they are progenitor-like cells (Jessen and Mirsky, 2019).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Jessen and Mirsky, 2019.

claim: Mouse SCPs express epidermal growth factor receptor+ (EGFR+).
source: Mouse SCPs also express epidermal growth factor receptor+ (EGFR+) and respond to EGF with limited self-renewal (Williams et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Williams et al., 2008.

claim: Mouse SCPs respond to EGF with limited self-renewal.
source: Mouse SCPs also express epidermal growth factor receptor+ (EGFR+) and respond to EGF with limited self-renewal (Williams et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Williams et al., 2008.

claim: EGFR+ cells that co-express the SC marker S100 account for about 1.8% human neurofibroma cells.
source: EGFR+ cells that co-express the SC marker S100 account for about 1.8% human neurofibroma cells (DeClue et al., 2000).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to DeClue et al., 2000.

claim: Human neurofibromas sorted for co-expression of the SC marker p75+ and EGFR show limited self-renewal in vitro.
source: The idea that these cells may be tumor-initiating cells is consistent with the finding that human neurofibromas sorted for co-expression of the SC marker p75+ and EGFR show limited self-renewal in vitro.
evidence: This is stated as an established finding in the field.

claim: EGFR-dependent Nf1-/- SCPs show increased self-renewal.
source: Also, EGFR-dependent Nf1-/- SCPs show increased self-renewal and form neurofibromas upon transplantation (Joseph et al., 2008; Williams et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Joseph et al., 2008 and Williams et al., 2008.

claim: EGFR-dependent Nf1-/- SCPs form neurofibromas upon transplantation.
source: Also, EGFR-dependent Nf1-/- SCPs show increased self-renewal and form neurofibromas upon transplantation (Joseph et al., 2008; Williams et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Joseph et al., 2008 and Williams et al., 2008.

claim: Neurofibromas contain progenitor-like cells which depend on EGFR for self-renewal.
source: Together, these studies suggest the presence of progenitor-like cells in neurofibromas, which depend on EGFR for self-renewal.
evidence: This is inferred from the cited studies about EGFR+ cells in neurofibromas.

claim: MPNST cells re-acquire EGFR expression that is absent in mature SC.
source: EGFR signaling may also play additional roles in transformed SCs, as MPNST cells re-acquire EGFR expression that is absent in mature SC (DeClue et al., 2000).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to DeClue et al., 2000.

claim: SCs associated with a single large-diameter axonal segment form myelin.
source: When associated with a single large-diameter axonal segment SCs form myelin.
evidence: This is established knowledge about SC biology.

claim: SCs associated with multiple smaller diameter axons become non-myelinating Remak cells.
source: SCs associated with multiple smaller diameter axons become non-myelinating Remak cells (Mirsky et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Mirsky et al., 2008.

claim: Neurofibroma SCs show a dramatic change in Remak SC morphology, bundling one or two few axons.
source: Neurofibroma SCs show a dramatic change in Remak SC morphology, bundling one or two few axons (Erlandson and Woodruff, 1982; Zheng et al., 2008), rather than up to 20 small diameter axons in WT nerve Remak bundles (Harty and Monk, 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Erlandson and Woodruff, 1982 and Zheng et al., 2008.

claim: WT nerve Remak bundles contain up to 20 small diameter axons.
source: Neurofibroma SCs show a dramatic change in Remak SC morphology, bundling one or two few axons (Erlandson and Woodruff, 1982; Zheng et al., 2008), rather than up to 20 small diameter axons in WT nerve Remak bundles (Harty and Monk, 2017).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Harty and Monk, 2017.

claim: Elevation of EGFR in WT SCPs and SCs is sufficient to mimic the nerve disruption phenotype.
source: Notably, while neurofibromas rarely form, elevation of EGFR in WT SCPs and SCs is sufficient to mimic this nerve disruption phenotype (Ling et al., 2005).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Ling et al., 2005.

claim: The NF1 gene encodes neurofibromin, a GTPase activating protein that accelerates the hydrolysis of RAS-GTP to its inactive GDP-bound form downstream of EGFR.
source: The NF1 gene encodes neurofibromin, a GTPase activating protein that accelerates the hydrolysis of RAS-GTP to its inactive GDP-bound form downstream of EGFR (Simanshu et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Simanshu et al., 2017.

claim: Loss of neurofibromin in SCs causes increases in GTP-bound RAS.
source: In SCs, loss of neurofibromin causes increases in GTP-bound RAS (Kim et al., 1995; Sherman et al., 2000), and RAS-GTP stimulates the mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) pathway and other downstream pathways, including deregulation of the PI3K-AKT signaling (Dasgupta et al., 2005; Johannessen et al., 2008; Patmore et al., 2012; Keng et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Kim et al., 1995 and Sherman et al., 2000.

claim: RAS-GTP stimulates the mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) pathway.
source: In SCs, loss of neurofibromin causes increases in GTP-bound RAS (Kim et al., 1995; Sherman et al., 2000), and RAS-GTP stimulates the mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) pathway and other downstream pathways, including deregulation of the PI3K-AKT signaling (Dasgupta et al., 2005; Johannessen et al., 2008; Patmore et al., 2012; Keng et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Dasgupta et al., 2005; Johannessen et al., 2008; Patmore et al., 2012; Keng et al., 2012.

claim: RAS-GTP causes deregulation of the PI3K-AKT signaling.
source: In SCs, loss of neurofibromin causes increases in GTP-bound RAS (Kim et al., 1995; Sherman et al., 2000), and RAS-GTP stimulates the mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) pathway and other downstream pathways, including deregulation of the PI3K-AKT signaling (Dasgupta et al., 2005; Johannessen et al., 2008; Patmore et al., 2012; Keng et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Dasgupta et al., 2005; Johannessen et al., 2008; Patmore et al., 2012; Keng et al., 2012.

claim: Loss of NF1 causes reduced levels of cyclic AMP (cAMP) in Nf1 mutant mouse, fly and zebrafish.
source: Loss of NF1 also causes reduced levels of cyclic AMP (cAMP) in Nf1 mutant mouse, fly and zebrafish (Hegedus et al., 2007; Tong et al., 2002; Wolman et al., 2014; Anastasaki and Gutmann, 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Hegedus et al., 2007; Tong et al., 2002; Wolman et al., 2014; Anastasaki and Gutmann, 2014.

claim: Neurofibromin shares homology with the yeast proteins Ira1 and Ira2.
source: Neurofibromin shares homology with the yeast proteins Ira1 and Ira2, which are inhibitory regulators of the RAS-cAMP adenylyl cyclase pathway, but no evidence shows a direct role for NF1 or IRA proteins in direct regulation of cAMP in mammals (Ballester et al., 1990; Martin et al., 1990; Xu et al., 1990).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Ballester et al., 1990; Martin et al., 1990; Xu et al., 1990.

claim: Ira1 and Ira2 are inhibitory regulators of the RAS-cAMP adenylyl cyclase pathway.
source: Neurofibromin shares homology with the yeast proteins Ira1 and Ira2, which are inhibitory regulators of the RAS-cAMP adenylyl cyclase pathway, but no evidence shows a direct role for NF1 or IRA proteins in direct regulation of cAMP in mammals (Ballester et al., 1990; Martin et al., 1990; Xu et al., 1990).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Ballester et al., 1990; Martin et al., 1990; Xu et al., 1990.

claim: No evidence shows a direct role for NF1 or IRA proteins in direct regulation of cAMP in mammals.
source: Neurofibromin shares homology with the yeast proteins Ira1 and Ira2, which are inhibitory regulators of the RAS-cAMP adenylyl cyclase pathway, but no evidence shows a direct role for NF1 or IRA proteins in direct regulation of cAMP in mammals (Ballester et al., 1990; Martin et al., 1990; Xu et al., 1990).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Ballester et al., 1990; Martin et al., 1990; Xu et al., 1990.

claim: Reducing cAMP drove formation of brain tumors in cells lacking Nf1.
source: It is unclear how, or if, regulation of cAMP is relevant to neurofibroma initiation or growth but reducing cAMP drove formation of brain tumors in cells lacking Nf1 (Warrington et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Warrington et al., 2010.

claim: P2ry14 is activated by extracellular UDP and UDP-sugars.
source: P2ry14 is activated by extracellular UDP and UDP-sugars and signal through Gi to inhibit adenylate cyclase (AC), decreasing cAMP (Abbracchio and Ceruti, 2006; Conroy et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Abbracchio and Ceruti, 2006 and Conroy et al., 2016.

claim: P2ry14 signals through Gi to inhibit adenylate cyclase (AC), decreasing cAMP.
source: P2ry14 is activated by extracellular UDP and UDP-sugars and signal through Gi to inhibit adenylate cyclase (AC), decreasing cAMP (Abbracchio and Ceruti, 2006; Conroy et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Abbracchio and Ceruti, 2006 and Conroy et al., 2016.

claim: P2ry14 regulates homeostasis of hematopoietic stem/progenitor cells.
source: Intriguingly, P2ry14 regulates homeostasis of hematopoietic stem/progenitor cells (Cho et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Cho et al., 2014.

claim: Satellite glial cells and SCs have been reported to express P2ry14 in vitro.
source: Also, satellite glial cells and SCs have been reported to express P2ry14 in vitro (Patritti-Cram et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Patritti-Cram et al., 2021.

claim: P2ry14 knockout increased mouse survival in a neurofibroma mouse model.
source: In vivo, P2ry14 knockout increased mouse survival, decreased SC proliferation, improved nerve Remak bundle morphology, and decreased tumor initiation.
evidence: The manuscript presents Kaplan-Meier survival data showing increased survival in P2ry14-/-;Nf1fl/fl;DhhCre mice.

claim: P2ry14 knockout decreased SC proliferation in a neurofibroma mouse model.
source: In vivo, P2ry14 knockout increased mouse survival, decreased SC proliferation, improved nerve Remak bundle morphology, and decreased tumor initiation.
evidence: The manuscript presents Ki67 staining data showing decreased proliferation in P2ry14-/-;Nf1fl/fl;DhhCre mice.

claim: P2ry14 knockout improved nerve Remak bundle morphology in a neurofibroma mouse model.
source: In vivo, P2ry14 knockout increased mouse survival, decreased SC proliferation, improved nerve Remak bundle morphology, and decreased tumor initiation.
evidence: The manuscript presents electron microscopy data showing improved Remak bundle morphology in P2ry14-/-;Nf1fl/fl;DhhCre mice.

claim: P2ry14 knockout decreased tumor initiation in a neurofibroma mouse model.
source: In vivo, P2ry14 knockout increased mouse survival, decreased SC proliferation, improved nerve Remak bundle morphology, and decreased tumor initiation.
evidence: The manuscript presents data showing decreased neurofibroma number in P2ry14-/-;Nf1fl/fl;DhhCre mice.

claim: Pharmacological elevation of cAMP diminished NF1 deficient SCP self-renewal in vitro.
source: Pharmacological elevation of cAMP diminished NF1 deficient SCP self-renewal in vitro and reduced SC proliferation in neurofibroma bearing mice in vivo.
evidence: The manuscript presents sphere formation assay data showing reduced self-renewal with rolipram treatment.

claim: Pharmacological elevation of cAMP reduced SC proliferation in neurofibroma bearing mice in vivo.
source: Pharmacological elevation of cAMP diminished NF1 deficient SCP self-renewal in vitro and reduced SC proliferation in neurofibroma bearing mice in vivo.
evidence: The manuscript presents Ki67 staining data showing reduced proliferation after rolipram treatment in vivo.

claim: P2ry14 mRNA is elevated in p75+/EGFR+ SCP-like tumor-initiating cells compared to p75+/EGFR- SCs.
source: Microarray heatmap shows P2ry14 receptor expression in p75+/EGFR+ SCP-like tumor-initiating cells derived from human plexiform neurofibroma tumor cells compared to p75+/EGFR- SCP-like cells.
evidence: Figure 1A shows microarray data comparing P2ry14 expression between cell populations.

claim: Human neurofibroma SCPs show a 1.9-fold increase of P2ry14 protein compared to human SCs.
source: Western blot of human Schwann cells and neurofibroma SCP shows the latter has a 1.9-fold increase in P2ry14 protein expression.
evidence: Figure 1B shows Western blot quantification of P2ry14 protein levels.

claim: P2ry14 protein is expressed on membranes of myelinating SCs in human neurofibroma tissue sections.
source: Anti-P2ry14 staining also showed P2ry14 protein membranes of myelinating SCs in human neurofibroma tissue sections (Figure 1C).
evidence: Figure 1C shows immunohistochemistry staining of P2ry14 in human neurofibroma tissue.

claim: On average, 23.4% of p75+/EGFR+/P2ry14- cells formed spheres.
source: FACS analysis (of cells from three additional neurofibroma tumors) showed that on average p75+/EGFR+/P2ry14- cells formed spheres at a frequency of 23.4%, while 64.8% of p75+/EGFR+/P2ry14+ cells formed spheres.
evidence: The manuscript presents quantitative data from FACS-sorted sphere formation assays.

claim: 64.8% of p75+/EGFR+/P2ry14+ cells formed spheres.
source: FACS analysis (of cells from three additional neurofibroma tumors) showed that on average p75+/EGFR+/P2ry14- cells formed spheres at a frequency of 23.4%, while 64.8% of p75+/EGFR+/P2ry14+ cells formed spheres.
evidence: The manuscript presents quantitative data from FACS-sorted sphere formation assays.

claim: p75+/EGFR+/P2ry14+ cells maintained their significantly enhanced ability to form spheres in vitro for three passages.
source: The p75+/EGFR+/P2ry14 + cells maintained their significantly enhanced ability to form spheres in vitro for three passages (Figure 1G and H).
evidence: Figure 1H shows quantification of sphere formation across three passages.

claim: P2ry14 is overexpressed in human neurofibroma SCPs in vitro.
source: Thus, P2ry14 is overexpressed in human neurofibroma SCPs in vitro, and marks SCP with the potential to self-renew in vitro.
evidence: This conclusion is based on the microarray, Western blot, and sphere formation data presented.

claim: P2ry14 marks SCP with the potential to self-renew in vitro.
source: Thus, P2ry14 is overexpressed in human neurofibroma SCPs in vitro, and marks SCP with the potential to self-renew in vitro.
evidence: This conclusion is based on the sphere formation data showing enhanced self-renewal in P2ry14+ cells.

claim: Treatment with PPTN reduced the percentage of Nf1-/- mouse SCPs that formed spheres.
source: We found that treatment with PPTN reduced the percentage of Nf1-/- mouse SCPs that formed spheres, but had little effect on WT SCPs, consistent with a role in Nf1 mutant SCP self-renewal (Figure 2A).
evidence: Figure 2A shows quantification of sphere formation after PPTN treatment.

claim: PPTN had little effect on WT SCP sphere formation.
source: We found that treatment with PPTN reduced the percentage of Nf1-/- mouse SCPs that formed spheres, but had little effect on WT SCPs, consistent with a role in Nf1 mutant SCP self-renewal (Figure 2A).
evidence: Figure 2A shows quantification of sphere formation after PPTN treatment.

claim: The optimal concentration of the P2ry14 inhibitor (PPTN) is 300 nM.
source: Dose-response analysis confirmed that the optimal concentration of the P2ry14 inhibitor (PPTN) is 300 nM; as 500 nM PPTN was toxic (Figure 2—figure supplement 2A–F).
evidence: Figure 2—figure supplement 2 shows dose-response data for PPTN.

claim: 500 nM PPTN was toxic to SCPs.
source: Dose-response analysis confirmed that the optimal concentration of the P2ry14 inhibitor (PPTN) is 300 nM; as 500 nM PPTN was toxic (Figure 2—figure supplement 2A–F).
evidence: Figure 2—figure supplement 2 shows toxicity at 500 nM PPTN.

claim: shP2ry14 treated cells showed reduced P2ry14 mRNA.
source: shP2ry14 treated cells showed reduced P2ry14 mRNA (Figure 2B) and P2ry14 protein (Figure 2C).
evidence: Figure 2B shows RT-PCR data demonstrating reduced P2ry14 mRNA after shRNA treatment.

claim: shP2ry14 treated cells showed reduced P2ry14 protein.
source: shP2ry14 treated cells showed reduced P2ry14 mRNA (Figure 2B) and P2ry14 protein (Figure 2C).
evidence: Figure 2C shows Western blot data demonstrating reduced P2ry14 protein after shRNA treatment.

claim: WT shP2ry14 shows a 0.4-fold decrease of P2ry14 protein compared to WT shNT.
source: WT shP2ry14 show a 0.4-fold decrease of P2ry14 protein compared to WT shNT.
evidence: Figure 2C shows Western blot quantification of P2ry14 protein levels.

claim: Nf1-/- shP2ry14 shows a 0.5-fold decrease of P2ry14 protein compared to Nf1-/- shNT.
source: Nf1-/- shP2ry14 show a 0.5-fold decrease compared to Nf1-/-.
evidence: Figure 2C shows Western blot quantification of P2ry14 protein levels.

claim: Sphere formation was significantly decreased in Nf1-/- SCPs treated with P2ry14 shRNA.
source: Sphere formation was significantly decreased in Nf1-/- SCPs but not WT treated with P2ry14 shRNA, and this phenotype also persisted for three passages (Figure 2D).
evidence: Figure 2D shows quantification of sphere formation after shP2ry14 treatment.

claim: Sphere formation was not significantly decreased in WT SCPs treated with P2ry14 shRNA.
source: Sphere formation was significantly decreased in Nf1-/- SCPs but not WT treated with P2ry14 shRNA, and this phenotype also persisted for three passages (Figure 2D).
evidence: Figure 2D shows quantification of sphere formation after shP2ry14 treatment.

claim: The decreased sphere formation phenotype after P2ry14 shRNA treatment persisted for three passages.
source: Sphere formation was significantly decreased in Nf1-/- SCPs but not WT treated with P2ry14 shRNA, and this phenotype also persisted for three passages (Figure 2D).
evidence: Figure 2D shows quantification of sphere formation across three passages.

claim: p-PKA substrate phosphorylation increased in WT SCPs after shP2ry14 treatment.
source: p-PKA substrate phosphorylation increased in WT and Nf1-/- SCPs shP2ry14 treated cells.
evidence: Figure 2E shows Western blot data of pPKA substrate phosphorylation after shP2ry14 treatment.

claim: p-PKA substrate phosphorylation increased in Nf1-/- SCPs after shP2ry14 treatment.
source: p-PKA substrate phosphorylation increased in WT and Nf1-/- SCPs shP2ry14 treated cells.
evidence: Figure 2E shows Western blot data of pPKA substrate phosphorylation after shP2ry14 treatment.

claim: WT shP2ry14 shows a 1.43-fold increase in pPKA after P2ry14 knockdown.
source: WT shP2ry14 shows a 1.43-fold increase in pPKA after P2ry14 knockdown.
evidence: Figure 2E shows Western blot quantification of pPKA substrate phosphorylation.

claim: Nf1-/- cells have a 1.31-fold increase in pPKA expression after P2ry14 knockdown.
source: Nf1-/- cells have a 1.31-fold increase in pPKA expression after P2ry14 knockdown.
evidence: Figure 2E shows Western blot quantification of pPKA substrate phosphorylation.

claim: In Nf1-/- SCPs, knockdown of P2ry14 increased levels of pPKA to those in WT shNT levels.
source: Importantly, in Nf1-/- SCPs knockdown of P2ry14 increased levels of pPKA to those in WT shNT levels (Figure 2E).
evidence: Figure 2E shows Western blot data comparing pPKA levels across conditions.

claim: Treatment with 1 µM rolipram decreased Nf1-/- SCP self-renewal.
source: Treatment with 1 µM rolipram or 300 nM of the P2ry14 inhibitor (PPTN) decreased Nf1-/- SCP self-renewal; the combination showed additional effect, largely at early passage (Figure 2F).
